<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="תמוז_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518919340_theRebbe_24" batchId="meluket-_D7_AA_D7_9E_D7_95_D7_96_meluket__BH_POST_1766518919340_theRebbe_24__p003">
  <section v="6">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section questions the connection between the thirteen hermeneutical principles and the revelation of new matters in Torah study.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And one must understand what is said at the beginning of the matter, that through the thirteen principles by which the Torah is expounded, new matters are revealed.</t>
    <t s="1">For seemingly,</t>
    <t s="2">the connection of the thirteen principles by which the Torah is expounded to what was discussed above—that through the Torah of the many a higher supernal light is drawn down—</t>
    <t s="3">is,</t>
    <t s="4">that these thirteen principles correspond to the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy,</t>
    <t s="5">and the drawing down of the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy is primarily specifically through the study of Torah in public,</t>
    <t s="6">and what relevance is there here that through the thirteen principles by which the Torah is expounded, new matters are revealed?</t>
  </section>
  <section v="7">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that through studying Torah with the thirteen hermeneutical principles, one draws down the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy, which are above the Torah, thereby revealing new matters.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And one may explain this as follows:</t>
    <t s="1">The difference between Torah and prayer is,</t>
    <t s="2">that prayer is when a person requests and prays, and the drawing down from Above</t>
    <t s="3">(that the Holy One, blessed be He, fulfills his request)</t>
    <t s="4">is accomplished through the prayer,</t>
    <t s="5">but not so with the occupation of Torah,</t>
    <t s="6">since the Torah that one learns is the word of G-d</t>
    <t s="7">(which exists even before the person's occupation with Torah),</t>
    <t s="8">therefore the effect accomplished through the occupation of Torah is seemingly that the Torah and the Ein Sof clothed within it be drawn down to the person.</t>
    <t s="9">And based on this, one could say,</t>
    <t s="10">that the superiority of the Torah of the many over the Torah of an individual is</t>
    <t s="11">(primarily)</t>
    <t s="12">only in regard to the person engaged in Torah study.</t>
    <t s="13">For although the discourse states that the superiority of Torah in public is</t>
    <t s="14">(not only in the person's reception,</t>
    <t s="15">that the Torah is acquired by him more,</t>
    <t s="16">but also)</t>
    <t s="17">in the drawing down from Above</t>
    <t s="18">(as above, section 2),</t>
    <t s="19">that through the study of Torah in public a higher supernal light is drawn down,</t>
    <t s="20">nevertheless, one could say,</t>
    <t s="21">that the entire matter of Torah study is that through the study, the light of the Torah</t>
    <t s="22">(which exists even before the study)</t>
    <t s="23">shines to the person who studies it,</t>
    <t s="24">and through the study of Torah in public, a more elevated light is revealed to the person.</t>
    <t s="25">And therefore the discourse brings that through the thirteen principles by which the Torah is expounded, new matters are revealed.</t>
    <t s="26">For just as prayer draws down a new will,</t>
    <t s="27">"May it be His will"31,</t>
    <t s="28">so too with Torah,</t>
    <t s="29">through the study of Torah according to the thirteen principles by which the Torah is expounded, new matters are revealed.</t>
    <t s="30">And the reason for this is,</t>
    <t s="31">for the thirteen principles by which the Torah is expounded correspond to the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy,</t>
    <t s="32">which are above the Torah.</t>
    <t s="33">For Torah is the wisdom of the Holy One, blessed be He,</t>
    <t s="34">the beginning of the chain of descent,</t>
    <t s="35">and the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy are above the chain of descent.</t>
    <t s="36">And through a person studying Torah according to the thirteen principles, he draws down into the Torah</t>
    <t s="37">(the chain of descent)</t>
    <t s="38">the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy which are above the chain of descent,</t>
    <t s="39">and through this, new matters are drawn into the Torah32.</t>
    <t s="40">And this is that through the study of Torah in public, a higher supernal light is drawn down from Above,</t>
    <t s="41">for the drawing down of the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy through Torah study is primarily specifically through the study of Torah in public,</t>
    <t s="42">meaning that the level of the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy drawn down through the study of Torah in public is a more elevated level.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="8">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the drawing down through the prayer of the many is not commensurate with their arousal, and likewise the drawing down through the Torah of the many is not commensurate with their study.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">D)</t>
    <t s="1">And the discourse continues33</t>
    <t s="2">with a further superiority in the prayer of the many,</t>
    <t s="3">that the drawing down from Above through the prayer of the many is not commensurate with the measure of their arousal from below.</t>
    <t s="4">For in addition to the fact that the arousal from below of the prayer of the many reaches a higher level, and therefore draws down a more elevated drawing down,</t>
    <t s="5">behold, through the prayer of the many a drawing down is drawn from Above that is not commensurate with the measure of the arousal from below,</t>
    <t s="6">nor even commensurate with the measure of the arousal from below of the many.</t>
    <t s="7">For this is what our sages, of blessed memory, said34</t>
    <t s="8">that the prayer of the many throughout all the days of the year is like the prayer of an individual during the Ten Days of Repentance,</t>
    <t s="9">that just as the drawing down through the prayer of an individual during the Ten Days of Repentance is not commensurate with the measure of his elevation</t>
    <t s="10">[therefore it is specifically during the Ten Days of Repentance,</t>
    <t s="11">because the Ten Days of Repentance are a time of will],</t>
    <t s="12">so too is the drawing down through the prayer of the many</t>
    <t s="13">(throughout all the days of the year),</t>
    <t s="14">which is not commensurate with the measure of the elevation</t>
    <t s="15">(nor even commensurate with the measure of the elevation of the many).</t>
    <t s="16">And so too with the Torah of the many,</t>
    <t s="17">that the drawing down through the study of the Torah of the many is not commensurate with the measure of the study of the many.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
